content.content: Apply these criteria to the dependent's recorded decision node, reading it against the prerequisite; nothing runs. A placeholder or empty commitment or rationale leaves the check with no recorded subject and fails naming the placeholder. (1) Bound and full viewport-change cost under active emphasis: the decision must commit to expressing selection emphasis so that applying one and the same viewport change costs the same however many elements the emphasis dims or brightens, and its recorded account must connect how emphasis is expressed to why a viewport change does no work proportional to the dimmed or brightened set. The account must cover the full cost of a viewport change through to the displayed surface — not only the step that initially applies or clears selection emphasis, and not only the write that updates the viewport transform — and must exclude any per-dimmed-element or per-brightened-element presentation, compositing, paint, layout or style-recalculation work provoked when the viewport moves or scales, as well as any per-element walk or update during a viewport change. Fail if the decision bounds only selection changes while leaving subsequent viewport changes under active emphasis unbounded, if it stops at the viewport-transform write and leaves host presentation work per dimmed or brightened element unaccounted for, or if it asserts the cost relation without connecting it to how emphasis is expressed, naming the gap. (2) Licence and non-contradiction: no element of the decision may contradict the prerequisite — in particular, no part may permit a viewport change's cost to grow with the number of dimmed, brightened or visible elements, or drop the interactive panel — and the decision must elaborate the prerequisite on how selection emphasis behaves across a viewport change rather than merely restating the prerequisite's general rule. Every clause must be licensed by the prerequisite's cost condition and must not require a rule the prerequisite does not state (a latency or frame budget, an element-count or node-count ceiling, a library, file or protocol, or a host other than the panel). Fail on any contradicting element, vacuous restatement, or unlicensed rule, naming it. (3) No substitute goal: the decision must not swap the prerequisite's cost-independence bound for a different goal — a frame-rate target, a latency budget, an element-count or node-count threshold, throttling or dropping viewport updates, or a visual or rendering technique adopted for its own sake without tying it to keeping viewport-change cost independent of the number of dimmed or brightened elements. Fail on any substituted goal, naming it. (4) Decidability: from the recorded statement alone, a reviewer must be able to name the refuting observation without supplying a rule of their own — two occurrences of the same viewport change under selection emphasis with different numbers of dimmed or brightened elements whose cost differs, or an emphasis expression that introduces work per dimmed or brightened element on a viewport change. Fail if no such observation can be named from the statement.
content.rationale: Both endpoints are inline prose commitments at the natural layer: the prerequisite fixes that a user interaction's cost follows what that interaction changed rather than the number of visible nodes, and the dependent elaborates that condition for how selection emphasis is expressed across a viewport change. The edge therefore sits in the evaluation matrix's natural-to-natural gate cell, where the check is applied by reading the dependent against the prerequisite and nothing runs. Because the prerequisite states a cost relation, non-violation is not settled by checking for surface verbal contradiction alone: a selection emphasis mechanism can apply its classes or styles incrementally when selection changes and update only a single viewport transform when panning or zooming, yet still express dimming or brightening in a way whose host presentation or compositing work on every viewport change scales with the number of dimmed or brightened elements — and since the dimmed set grows with the visible graph, that term makes one and the same viewport change cost more when more nodes are visible. The criterion therefore checks that the dependent entails the prerequisite's bound across the full cost of a viewport change under active emphasis, connects that bound to how emphasis is expressed rather than merely asserting it, contradicts nothing in the prerequisite, imports no unrecorded rule or substitute goal, and stays decidable from its recorded statement alone. It demands no particular wording, sentence order or code-layer artifact, and any failing element or gap is named only in the check's output.
